questions.q: Why did LTV Global reject a fully centralized operating model?
options: A small central program team would become a bottleneck for a company with three regions and six business units
Centralized models are illegal under UK GDPR
LTV Global has no executive sponsor to lead a centralized model
A centralized model was never considered
questions.explain: The lesson explains that fully centralizing every decision in Dana Whitfield's small program team doesn't scale across LTV Global's regions and business units.

questions.q: Why did LTV Global reject a fully decentralized operating model?
options: That is essentially what already existed before the program started, and it's what caused the Lesson 1 incident
Decentralized models are always faster, so it was rejected for being too slow
LTV Global has no business units to decentralize into
It would have required firing the data stewards
questions.explain: The lesson states a fully decentralized model describes the pre-program status quo — three disconnected systems with no one accountable for reconciliation.

questions.q: What operating model shape does LTV Global adopt, and what does it combine?
options: A federated hybrid model — a small central office for standards and cross-domain decisions, with domain owners keeping day-to-day authority
A purely centralized model with no domain owners
A purely decentralized model with no central office at all
No operating model was chosen; the program remains informal
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly names the federated hybrid model as the chosen shape, combining central standards with distributed domain-level ownership.

questions.q: What kind of issue reaches the monthly Data Governance Council, per this lesson?
options: An authoritative-source dispute nobody below that level can settle, a KPI missed two months running, or a new CDE candidate
Every single data entry error across the company, no matter how small
Only issues related to the Harbor warehouse system
Nothing ever reaches the council; it exists only on paper
questions.explain: The lesson lists these specific escalation triggers — unresolved authoritative-source disputes, missed KPI targets, and new CDE candidates like DateOfBirth — as what reaches the council.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what happens to deliverables like the landscape inventory and glossary now that the operating model exists?
options: They are maintained on an ongoing basis by the governance office, not treated as one-time documents
They are deleted now that the operating model is in place
They are frozen permanently and never updated again
They are handed over entirely to an outside vendor
questions.explain: The lesson's closing section states explicitly that every earlier deliverable is maintained going forward, using DateOfBirth's re-classification as a concrete example.
